decision_reason: Retain the nine A1 concepts and add wrist_orientation_variability to distinguish local hand reorientation from global posture and overall rotational motion. This offers a plausible additional contrast for writing versus eating soup, which differ in only motion_intensity in A1, and a complementary description of folding clothes versus feeding activities. Stairs and clapping have the weakest supplied seen coverage, but their locomotor and impact semantics already have seen anchors; additional activity-specific dimensions would have uncertain predictability. Standing versus sitting remains difficult because user-carried phone orientation does not uniquely identify load-bearing posture. The supplied distances guide these priorities but are not evidence of recognition performance.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: wrist_orientation_variability
attributes.definition: Extent of change in the wrist-worn watch's gravity-relative orientation within a window, reflecting local wrist and forearm reorientation rather than global body posture or rotation about gravity alone.

levels.Low: Gravity-relative wrist orientation remains nearly constant.
levels.Medium: Gravity-relative wrist orientation changes through a moderate angular range.
levels.High: Gravity-relative wrist orientation changes through a broad angular range.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall movement energy in phone and watch signals. It preserves transferable quiet-versus-vigorous contrasts, including stairs relative to walking and clapping relative to dribbling (basketball). Effort, movement style and phone placement can blur adjacent levels; energy alone does not identify an activity.

cadence: G6 supports the rate of repeated stepping or hand-action cycles. Walking and jogging anchor locomotor repetition, while dribbling (basketball) anchors repeated upper-limb action for clapping. Pauses, short windows and multiple nested movement cycles can obscure the meaningful repetition rate.

smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid changes in movement rather than isolated impacts. This retains a transferable distinction between comparatively continuous writing or handling movements and repeatedly abrupt clapping, with eating soup and dribbling (basketball) as anchors. Movement speed, pauses and sensor vibration can alter apparent smoothness.

impulsiveness: G10 supports brief abrupt changes associated with hand contact or foot loading. Clapping can transfer impact semantics from dribbling (basketball) and playing catch w/tennis ball without adding a clap-specific concept. Soft contacts, watch-side participation and incidental knocks can weaken or mimic this evidence.

posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative mean orientation, potentially providing indirect posture evidence when the phone follows the load-bearing body. Preserve the existing sitting-to-standing semantic contrast rather than inventing a second posture cue. Unknown phone placement, upright sitting and local wrist motion make global posture inference ambiguous; wrist orientation alone is not evidence of global inclination.

posture_variability: G12 supports changes in gravity-relative orientation when a carried phone follows body configuration. It preserves the distinction between stable posture and body adjustments in stairs or folding clothes, with kicking (soccer ball) providing a seen example of substantial adjustment. Loose phone carriage and isolated limb motion can masquerade as global posture changes.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular movement observed by phone or watch gyroscopes. It retains broad rotation semantics transferable from drinking from cup and brushing teeth to eating pasta and folding clothes. Small rapid rotations and broad slow rotations can produce overlapping overall prominence, and the watched hand may not perform the principal action.

translational_motion: G13 supports short-window evidence of progression, allowing stairs to share locomotor semantics with walking and jogging rather than requiring a stair-specific elevation attribute. Inertial proxies do not establish absolute displacement or elevation; repetitive stationary limb movement and carriage variation can confuse the evidence.

motion_regularity: G11 supports recurrence and temporal predictability independently of repetition speed. It retains a useful distinction between structured eating pasta and less predictable folding clothes, with feeding activities and drinking from cup as seen anchors. Short windows, voluntary pauses and individually consistent folding routines can blur these semantic expectations.

wrist_orientation_variability: G12 supports gravity-relative orientation changes at the watch, with G2 providing corroborating angular-motion evidence. Near-surface writing can involve limited wrist inclination change despite ongoing small rotations, whereas eating soup involves hand transport and reorientation; this offers an additional contrast beyond their single A1 intensity difference. Drinking from cup, eating soup and typing provide seen examples of differing local orientation behavior. The concept also describes reorientation during folding clothes without presuming that it always separates folding clothes from eating pasta. Dynamic acceleration, watched-hand choice, utensil technique and window duration can obscure angular range; rotation about gravity alone does not increase this attribute. These limitations favor one broad local-orientation dimension rather than fine-grained manipulation labels.

semantic_redundancy_review: The ten attributes retain distinct physical meanings. Cadence is repetition rate, whereas motion_regularity is predictability. Smoothness describes sustained rapid fluctuations, whereas impulsiveness describes isolated peaks. Motion_intensity concerns overall energy, not orientation excursion. Rotational_motion concerns angular-motion prominence; wrist_orientation_variability concerns the gravity-relative angular range explored locally and can remain low during rapid small rotations. Posture_inclination and posture_variability concern the global load-bearing configuration, not the wrist. Translational_motion concerns sustained progression, not local hand transport. These concepts can correlate without being interchangeable. No elevation, object identity, bilateral coordination or seated-leg configuration attribute is added because the supplied capabilities and unspecified phone carriage do not establish reliable observation of those distinctions.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
